chapter: Russell and Armstrong years, Goodman and the road
title: Racist confrontation at an Atlanta club
summary: At a rich club in Atlanta a drunken white patron threatened to shoot him until another white man intervened.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: You got yours? (LAUGHTER) I'm glad I sold mine. I went to Georgia. I played down there; I played this Newport Festival in Atlanta. I played there for rich people; it was very nice. I had a little trouble. One night with one guy - I had two weeks on this job. Rich people, so I mean, the negros would come in too. This white fellow used to come over and laugh and talk. He said, I'd like for you to go out and have a sandwich and a drink after you get through work. So the trumpet player was white. He said, it's O.K., I'll go with you. Beautiful man.... So the sun was up and he was high. He said, I'm getting tired of my wife driving you around and you don't know where you live. I said I'll give you the address. So the next night he came on and played. At intermission I got about a dozen tourists who said we know you from different

places over in Europe. "Come over and have a drink." So I looked up and here he come in. He was all right the first night so we laughed and talked. They didn't pay him no mind. So I hate for a white man to (ruin my evening.) So I was sitting there and he came over and he did this. He said, "You know what I'm going to name you, boy?" I said, "What?" He said, "A baldheaded nigger." I said, "You know what I'm going to name you, boy?" He said, "What?" I said, "Cracker motherf——r." And he turned every color! (LAUGHTER) So the other people they tried to ignore us so I said, well we'd better leave. There's a friend of mine I just got a letter from last week, from Decatur, Georgia. White fellow too. I mean, you can find good people every place. So he and his wife was waiting to say good night and here he comes in and sits down. So this fellow and his wife said, "Jay, we're going now. We're just waiting to say goodnight." And here he come and he sat down. So he said, "I'm going to shoot me a nigger tonight." So this white fellow, he just happened to think. He said, "I forgot. Let's go back and get a night cap." Maybe that saved a bullet out of my head. ( ? )
But do you think he was actually going to shoot you?
Who's going to take the chance?
Do you think it was because his wife was there?
There was nobody there but he and his wife and I'm walking down to the car lot, trying to walk away from him, and he's coming on out there with her. So this guy he happened
to think and that's when he said, "Go back and have a night cap." So they must have said something to the manager; they got him out of there.
